headline: Duration finally gave back a few basis points — and the dollar went up anyway, which means this is a funding squeeze, not a rate story.
summary: The rates shock did more than pause today; it partially reversed. The 2-year fell 10bp to 4.78%, the 5-year 8bp to 5.01%, the 10-year 5bp to 5.24%, and the 10-year real yield 5bp to 2.88%. MOVE dropped 2.1% to 108.13 and TLT closed +0.3%. The rates composite improved from -82 to -78. The front end led, so 2s10s steepened 5bp to 0.46 and 3m10y sits at 1.07, the 98th percentile of the year. That is the textbook shape of a market pricing cuts back in rather than a term-premium accident — but the level is still punishing: 10y at the 96th percentile, 30y 5.61% at the 97th, the 30-year mortgage pinned at 7.28% (100th percentile, +62bp on the month), MOVE still +38.8% on the month with z=2.11 and acceleration 1.59.

What changed is the dollar's character. Yesterday DXY rose with yields; today DXY rose 0.7% to 102.11 — 100th percentile, z=1.22, acceleration 0.98 — while every US yield fell. Rate differentials did not do that. EURUSD -0.8% to 1.1238 at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, GBPUSD -0.6%, AUDUSD -0.4%, CEW -0.6%, USDCAD z=1.40 with acceleration 1.25, and USDMXN +1.3% to 18.321 with z=2.98 and acceleration 2.38 — still the most extreme print on the board. AUDJPY, the cleanest risk cross, carries z=-1.78 with acceleration -1.79. Offshore equities paid immediately and harder than the US: Euro Stoxx -1.5%, FTSE -1.7%, CAC -1.6%, EWI -2.5%, EWP -2.3%, EPOL -2.4%, GREK -2.1%, ARGT -2.1%, EZA -1.8%, HSI -2.5%, EWW -1.9%. EFA/SPY fell another 1.2% and is at the 0th percentile of the year. Dollar composite -24.

Inside the US, today was not the usual narrow melt-up. Equal-weight beat cap-weight for once with real participation: RSP +0.5% against SPX +0.2%, MDY +1.0%, DJT +1.1%, XTN +1.3%, XLI +1.0%, PAVE +1.0%, BA +3.3%, CAT +1.9%. Energy led outright — XLE +2.0%, XOP +2.8%, CVX +1.4% — with WTI +2.7% to 92.89 and oil/gold +3.0% at the 83rd percentile. Electrification accelerated again: GEV +3.9% (acc 1.03), ETN +1.8% (+11.9% on the month, acc 1.54), GRID +1.0% turning up. Credit stopped bleeding: HYG unchanged at 76.90 with its z improving from -1.74 to -1.50, LQD +0.3%, BKLN +0.1%, credit & vol composite +26. Semis kept their bid — SMH +1.4% and +13.3% on the month, SOXX +15.3%, MU +3.0%, SMH/SPY z=1.73 acc 1.49 — and crypto turned up across the complex (BTC +1.3% to 84,633, +9.5% on the month; SOL +18.2%; MSTR +4.8% and +28.5%).

The damage rotated rather than healed. Breadth internals remain broken under the cosmetic bounce: RSP/SPY z=-1.91 at the 8th percentile, IWM/SPY -4.2% on the month at the 25th, QQQ/SPY z=1.70. The precious-and-hard-asset liquidation is now the fastest-moving thing on the board — GDX -1.2% with acceleration -2.50, GDXJ acc -2.29, GDX/GOLD acc -2.69, NEM acc -2.42, gold -5.0% on the month, silver -6.2%, XME -9.9%, REMX -17.4% at the 1st percentile, NLR -11.2% at the 0th. And today the defensive side cracked: XLV -1.3%, IBB -2.2%, XBI -2.0%, IHI -1.0%, NFLX -2.5% at the 0th percentile. Financials are still in open liquidation on the month (XLF -6.2%, BX -17.9%, GS -10.6%, IAI -7.6%) despite a 98th-percentile 3m10y curve. Risk regime -13, barely better than -14. The message: domestic reflation is re-emerging under a dollar that is squeezing everyone else.

good.text: First genuine duration relief in weeks, led by the front end: 2y -10bp to 4.78%, 5y -8bp to 5.01%, 10y -5bp to 5.24%, 10y real -5bp to 2.88%, MOVE -2.1% to 108.13, TLT +0.3%. 2s10s steepened 5bp to 0.46 — cuts getting priced, not term premium exploding.
Breadth bounced with actual participation for the first time: RSP +0.5% vs SPX +0.2%, MDY +1.0%, DJT +1.1%, XTN +1.3%, XLI +1.0%, PAVE +1.0%, BA +3.3%.

Energy and the real-economy cyclical complex led the tape: WTI +2.7% to 92.89 (+35.2% on the quarter), XLE +2.0%, XOP +2.8%, CVX +1.4%, CAT +1.9%. Growth pulse +17 and copper/gold at the 93rd percentile with acceleration 1.12.
Credit stopped bleeding. HYG flat at 76.90 with its 1m z-score improving from -1.74 to -1.50, LQD +0.3% after -2.6% on the month, BKLN +0.1%. Credit & vol composite +26.

AI/semis leadership intact and broadening across Asia supply chain: SMH +1.4% (+13.3% 1m), SOXX +15.3% 1m, MU +3.0%, TSM +0.7% (+11.2% 1m), CIBR +7.9% 1m, META +25.6% 1m with z=2.03 and acceleration 1.37.

Electrification capex accelerating and crypto flipping up: GEV +3.9% (acc 1.03), ETN +1.8% (+11.9% 1m, acc 1.54), GRID turning up; BTC +1.3% to 84,633 (+9.5% 1m) at only the 39th percentile, SOL +18.2% 1m, MSTR +4.8%.

bad.text: The dollar rose 0.7% to 102.11 — 100th percentile, acceleration 0.98 — on a day every US yield fell. That is dollar funding demand, not rate differentials. EURUSD -0.8% at the 0th percentile, USDMXN z=2.98/acc 2.38, USDCAD acc 1.25, CEW -0.6%, AUDJPY z=-1.78 with acceleration -1.79.

Offshore equities broke again and the gap is widening: Euro Stoxx -1.5%, FTSE -1.7%, CAC -1.6%, EWI -2.5%, EWP -2.3%, EPOL -2.4%, HSI -2.5%, EWW -1.9%, Sensex at the 0th percentile. EFA/SPY -1.2% and sitting at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks.

A 5bp rally doesn't fix the level. 30y 5.61% (97th pctile), 10y 5.24% (96th), 30-year mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile, 10y real +44bp on the month with acceleration 1.39, MOVE +38.8% on the month. Housing stays broken: ITB at the 8th pctile, XHB/SPY at the 3rd, HD at the 0th.

Breadth internals are still a shell: RSP/SPY z=-1.91 at the 8th percentile, IWM/SPY -4.2% on the month at the 25th, QQQ/SPY z=1.70 and 4.4% higher on the month. The index is still a chip trade wearing a market costume.

Hard assets are in accelerating liquidation, the fastest-moving negative on the board: GDX acc -2.50, GDXJ acc -2.29, GDX/GOLD acc -2.69, NEM acc -2.42, gold -5.0% and silver -6.2% on the month, XME -9.9%, REMX -17.4% (1st pctile), NLR -11.2% (0th pctile), URA -9.9%.

Today the defensives cracked while financials stayed in liquidation: XLV -1.3%, IBB -2.2%, XBI -2.0%, IHI -1.0%, NFLX -2.5% at the 0th percentile; XLF -6.2% on the month (rel -6.7%), BX -17.9%, GS -10.6%, IAI -7.6% despite 3m10y at the 98th percentile.

trades.name: Long SPY / short EFA
trades.line: Long SPY vs short EFA: dollar squeeze is an offshore problem
trades.expr: Buy SPY, short EFA, dollar-neutral notional 1:1. Add a short EWI/EWP leg against SPY for the levered-beta version.
trades.thesis: The dollar is rising while US yields fall. That is global dollar funding demand, and it taxes non-US earnings and non-US balance sheets far more than US ones. The US has domestic reflation (energy, industrials, semis) to offset; Europe just has the FX hit.
trades.trigger: DXY +0.7% to 102.11 at the 100th percentile on a day the 2y fell 10bp. EFA -1.0%, EFA/SPY -1.2% to the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, Euro Stoxx -1.5%, EWI -2.5%, EWP -2.3%, EURUSD at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: EURUSD closes back above 1.145 or DXY back under 100.5, with EFA/SPY reclaiming its 200-day (-5.2% away).
trades.target: Another 4-6% of relative underperformance in EFA/SPY; exit on a DXY acceleration z-score flip negative.

trades.name: 2s10s steepener
trades.line: Steepener: front end rallies 10bp, long end only 3bp
trades.expr: Long 2y Treasury futures (TU) vs short ultra-bond (WN), DV01-neutral; ETF proxy long SHY vs short TLT. Size 1 to 1.5 bp/day of curve.
trades.thesis: The relief in rates is a front-end story — growth deceleration and cuts getting re-priced — while term premium and supply keep the long end sticky. Bond vol rolling over from an extreme removes the convexity squeeze that had been flattening the curve mechanically.
trades.trigger: 2y -10bp to 4.78% vs 30y only -3bp to 5.61%; 2s10s +5bp to 0.46 and +15bp on the week; MOVE -2.1% to 108.13 off a z=2.11 extreme; 3m10y at 1.07, the 98th percentile.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 0.35, or a 10y real yield (2.88%) break above 3.05% that drags the front end back up with it.
trades.target: 2s10s to 0.75-0.85, roughly the level implied by 3m10y at 1.07.

trades.name: Energy equities (XLE/XOP)
trades.line: Long XLE and XOP: crude at 92.89, energy led the tape
trades.expr: Buy XLE core, XOP for beta, 2:1. Fund partially by shorting OIH, which is rolling over (-10.7% on the month, acc -1.28).
trades.thesis: Crude is up 35.2% on the quarter and 61.8% YTD with Brent at 102.51, yet XLE is only -2.6% on the month and energy's 3-month relative strength is +15.2% and still trending up. The equities have not discounted the strip, and oil/gold at +8.4% on the month says real-asset demand is rotating out of the metals and into the barrel.
trades.trigger: WTI +2.7% to 92.89, XLE +2.0%, XOP +2.8%, CVX +1.4%, XOM +0.7% — the biggest sector move on the board, on a day Europe fell 1.5%.
trades.stop: WTI closes below 85 (back under its 200-day region) or Brent loses 95; XLE relative-strength trend flips to down.
trades.target: XLE +10% and a close of the gap between XLE's -2.6% monthly and crude's +3.0%.

trades.name: US consumer discretionary
trades.line: Short XLY: 7.28% mortgage, HD at 0th pctile, MCD z=-2.39
trades.expr: Short XLY outright or buy Dec/Jan XLY puts ~5% OTM; single-name expression short HD and MCD against long SPY.
trades.thesis: The rate shock has already passed through to the household. The mortgage rate is at the top of its 52-week range and the consumer tape is confirming it name by name. Today's duration relief is 5bp — nowhere near enough to reverse 62bp of monthly mortgage damage before Q4 prints.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile; XLY -4.8% on the month at the 19th percentile with rel -5.3%; HD -11.0% on the month at the 0th percentile; MCD -11.2% with z=-2.39; NKE -7.8% at the 0th percentile; XRT/SPY at the 6th percentile; UBER -9.8%.
trades.stop: 10y sustains below 4.90% and the mortgage rate prints under 7.00%, or XLY/XLP turns up through its 200-day.
trades.target: XLY -8% absolute, or XLY/SPY down another 5%.

trades.name: Grid equipment vs power producers
trades.line: Long GEV+ETN vs short CEG+VST: sell the megawatt, buy the box
trades.expr: Equal-weight long GEV and ETN, short CEG and VST, beta-matched. Overlay long GRID vs short NLR for the ETF version.
trades.thesis: The electrification trade is bifurcating. Equipment makers monetise the capex backlog regardless of power prices; independent power producers are long duration and long power-price optimism, both of which are being repriced at 5.6% on the 30-year. Buy the order book, sell the asset.
trades.trigger: GEV +3.9% today with acceleration 1.03 and +9.9% on the month; ETN +1.8%, +11.9% on the month with acceleration 1.54; against CEG -7.6% on the month at the 14th percentile, VST at the 7th percentile and -13.0% YTD, NLR -11.2% at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: GEV/ETN acceleration z-scores roll negative, or CEG and VST reclaim their 200-days (currently -9.9% and -9.6% below).

trades.name: Bitcoin via IBIT
trades.line: Long IBIT: BTC turning up at only the 39th pctile of 52wks
trades.expr: Buy IBIT; higher-beta sleeve in MSTR sized at a third. Use a 10% stop on IBIT rather than options — implied is not the edge here.
trades.thesis: Crypto has quietly flipped to turning_up across every leg of the complex while still sitting in the bottom half of its 52-week range — the rare momentum trade without momentum pricing. A front-end rally that steepens the curve is the historical fuel; the dollar is the risk, and it is priced.
trades.trigger: BTC +1.3% to 84,633, +9.5% on the month and +35.3% on the quarter at only the 39th percentile; ETH +13.0% on the month, SOL +18.2%, IBIT +9.6%, MSTR +4.8% today and +28.5% on the month; ETH/BTC turning up. All six crypto series now carry a turning_up trend state.
trades.stop: BTC closes below 76,000 (through its 200-day, currently 14.6% below spot) or the complex reverts to a down trend state.

trades.name: Cheap S&P downside vs expensive bond vol
trades.line: Buy SPX puts: VIX 16.4 at 17th pctile vs MOVE z=2.11
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPX 5-7% OTM put spreads, or a Nov/Dec VIX 20/30 call spread. Finance by selling 1-month VIX futures or by overwriting a long-only semis book.
trades.thesis: The bond market is pricing a crisis and the equity market is pricing none. Equity vol is at the bottom of its range with index breadth at the 8th percentile — meaning a handful of semis names are holding up the index while the median stock, the banks and now health care all break. That is the exact configuration where a single AI-capex disappointment gaps the index.
trades.trigger: VIX 16.39 at the 17th percentile and VIX3M 18.58 at the 10th, against MOVE at 108.13 with z=2.11 and acceleration 1.59; SKEW -4.3% on the month; RSP/SPY z=-1.91; XLV -1.3%, IBB -2.2%, XBI -2.0% today — the defensive hedge is failing too.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY turns up through its 200-day and HYG reclaims 78 with a positive z-score; then the carry on long vol is not worth paying.
trades.target: VIX 24-26, or a 6-8% SPX drawdown from 7,666.
